# A full nonlinear perspective obstruction and its one-input repair calibration

This note compares two ACTUAL compatible contact continuations on the
same genuine critical three-fiber family. It proves that varying the
source parameter cannot give a strictly paying first variation for the
original symmetric continuation, but
the new one-input continuation does pay. It does not infer a universal
choice of continuation for arbitrary fibers.

## 1. Actual critical data

Let T=conv{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)}, of area V=9/2, and take fibers

    K_-1=aT, K_0=T, K_1=bT,
    a=19/20, b=21/20, a+b=2.

All midpoint contacts are tight. The complete all-normal theorem in
`candidate f89d52b54ff6950f`
gives actual global raw depth Q=6 at the middle centroid, total
M=5409/400, and beta=800/1803. The three canonical caps have common
integer tilt alpha=a-b=-1/10 and are all proper. Their actual response
weights are1/3, by the continuous vertex-permutation symmetry and equal
coareas. The corresponding relative barycentric thresholds are

    q_-1=17/57, q_0=1/3, q_1=23/63,                       (1)

all strictly between0 and1/2.

## 2. The entire old perspective family has nonpositive first-order payment

Allow an ARBITRARY finite nonnegative jointly continuous function psi(n,v)
on the unit-normal sphere times R^2, convex in v for each fixed normal n.
Use its common homothetic perspective
fields on the three fibers:

    Psi_z(n,r_z v)=r_z h_T(n) psi(n,v),
    (r_-1,r_0,r_1)=(a,1,b).                              (2)

The original two-input projective construction is included by taking
psi(n,v)=f(1+c dot v), for ANY parameter c and ANY common positive
finite convex f. No centroid normalization of c is needed for the
following obstruction. Weighted perspective Jensen makes (2) the same
compatible field class as the old source; its total and cap costs are
the actual surface first variations from the audited perspective source.

Parametrize any facet of T by t in[0,1] between its two vertices. The
three-cap profile restricted to a fiber of threshold q is

    W_q(t)=1/3+(1/3)1_[q,1-q](t).                         (3)

Its own-vertex cap misses that facet, and its other two caps give the
two indicated endpoint intervals. Under homothetic pullback, field times
surface measure scales by r_z^2. Put

    S=a^2+1+b^2,
    w(t)=[a^2 W_(q_-1)(t)+W_(q_0)(t)+b^2 W_(q_1)(t)]/S.

This function is symmetric about1/2 and nonincreasing on[1/2,1]. Its
mean is EXACTLY beta. Indeed integral W_q=2(1-q)/3, and the thresholds
in(1) give

    sum_z r_z^2(1-q_z)=2,
    integral_0^1 w=4/(3S)=beta.                           (4)

For any convex edge function g, its symmetric part
(g(1/2+s)+g(1/2-s))/2 is nondecreasing for0<=s<=1/2.
The opposite monotonicity of w gives reversed Chebyshev:

    integral_0^1 [w(t)-beta]g(t)dt<=0.                   (5)

For completeness, on the half interval the double integral of
[w(s)-w(t)][g_sym(s)-g_sym(t)] is nonpositive. Expanding it gives exactly
twice the interval length times the covariance; symmetry and(4) give(5).
No smoothness of g or strictness at the step boundaries is needed.

Apply(5) to each facet's actual restriction of psi, and multiply by
its positive constant h_T(n) times facet length and by S. Summing gives

    sum_j theta_j D_total(H_j) - beta D_total <=0.         (6)

Thus NO parameter c, and not even an arbitrary common convex rescaled
boundary field in(2), yields strict first-order normalized response descent for this
critical circuit. This is stronger than the a=0 affine-neutrality
calibration: the whole nonlinear symmetric-perspective continuation is
blocked on this actual example. Zero first variation does not exclude
higher-order finite descent. The obstruction also does not exclude
independently modifying the input fields or a different compatible path.

## 3. The one-input continuation gives a strict actual payment

Use the new one-input construction in Sections6--8 of
`candidate c56743c8d6824a18`.
At the current centroid source its parameter is zero. Eroding only the
smaller input with field2h_T, and the middle with field h_T, keeps the
larger input fixed. The radii are exactly

    a_e=a-2e, c_e=1-e, b_e=b.                              (7)

They retain the tight midpoint equality and positive bodies for small e.
The optimized canonical tilt is alpha_e=alpha-2e. Its common cap mass,
while the same proper branch remains active, is exactly

    Q_opt(e)=2c_e^2+(a_e+b)^2=6(1-e)^2.                   (8)

Keeping the ORIGINAL three closed caps instead gives

    Q_fixed(e)=Q_opt(e)+(alpha-alpha_e)^2
              =6(1-e)^2+4e^2.                           (9)

Thus threshold optimization is not needed for the strict first-order
payment: both versions have loss12. The total mass is

    M_e=5409/400-(261/10)e+(45/2)e^2.                    (10)

The exact loss efficiency and normalized response are

    12/(261/10)=40/87>4/9,
    -12+beta(261/10)=-252/601<0.                         (11)

For a fully finite check, e=1/1000 remains in the proper minimizing
branch. The all-normal formula still makes the middle globally deepest,
with actual normalized value147852/333245<800/1803. Even the fixed caps
give upper value2395204/5398569<800/1803; their cover of the middle plane
is unchanged, and the old endpoint isolation covers remain uniformly
slack. This is actual strict global descent, not merely a cap calculation.

After division by the common middle scale1-e, the endpoint radii still
sum to2 but their asymmetry strictly increases. This identifies the new
freedom: the one-input continuation varies the two relative endpoint
scales instead of applying a common convex profile to all normalized
fiber boundaries. The obstruction(6) therefore does not apply.

## 4. An exact all-dimensional homothetic cost identity

For a d-simplex T of volume V, put r_A=a, r_K=1 and r_B=2-a,
where d/(d+1)<a<=1. This strict lower bound makes the balanced
small-endpoint cut proper; it is essential to the following cap formula.
Normalize a canonical vertex functional to have vertex values d,-1,...,-1.
At the balanced proper endpoint tilt d(a-1), each original endpoint
cap has volume Gamma_d V, as does the middle cap. Under the one-input
radii path(a-2e,1-e,2-a), differentiation of the vertex-cap polynomial
gives total row loss3d Gamma_d V. The total volume loss is
dV(1+2a^(d-1)). Hence its ratio is

    3 Gamma_d/[1+2a^(d-1)] >= Gamma_d.                    (12)

This is a fixed proper-cap cost identity; global criticality of that
canonical menu is NOT asserted in arbitrary dimensions or radius ranges.
For the genuine planar instance above the required criticality and global
competing-center comparison are separately certified. Equation(12) gives
a concrete calibration of endpoint choice, not a general OC theorem.
